elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Revised sentence reads "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT ... EXCEED ...", replacing the one-way "TRUELINK'S LIABILITY" and the Section 3/4/7/11 scope limit, so the cap now runs to Client as well.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Operative text caps at "THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD" — no USD 1,000,000 floor and "paid" only, not "paid or payable". To reach preferred, insert "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable ... in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: No exclusion-of-damages language appears in the rendered clause, and the rationale confirms searches for consequential/indirect damages return nothing elsewhere in the Agreement. A mutual exclusion sentence would have to be added.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Carve-out parenthetical: "(OTHER THAN ... ITS BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS ...)", stated for "A PARTY" and therefore mutual.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list covers only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out appears in operative text.
"(OTHER THAN A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS ...)" — the broad Section 12(a) Client indemnity at p0071 is expressly outside the cap for either party.
"(OTHER THAN ... ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE ...)", now expressed as a party-neutral carve-out rather than TrueLink-only.
"(OTHER THAN ... OR ITS WILLFUL MISCONDUCT)", party-neutral and therefore mutual.
No fraud carve-out in the parenthetical; the drafter would need to add "its fraud" to the excluded matters.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out appears; the excluded matters stop at willful misconduct.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Nothing in the revised sentence states that Client's obligation to pay fees is not "damages" subject to the cap; that preferred sentence is absent.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT ..." — mutuality is on the face of the operative text, curing the walk-away condition of an uncapped Client against a capped TrueLink.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Retained existing basis: "THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD" — a 12-month fee measure, not an illusory fixed set-up fee.
Express carve-out "A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS" keeps indemnities outside the cap for both sides.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Express carve-out "ITS BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS" applies to either party.
Express carve-out "ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE", now mutual rather than TrueLink-only.
Express carve-out "OR ITS WILLFUL MISCONDUCT", now mutual.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete on the operative text alone: mutual "EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY" cap, retained 12-month fee basis, and a single parenthetical carving out indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct for both parties. Nothing is left to the margin comment.

Preferred is not reached and is correctly not claimed: missing USD 1,000,000 floor and "paid or payable", no mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion, and no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud or IP infringement, and no statement that Client's payment obligations are not capped damages. If escalating, add: "the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000"; a mutual exclusion of indirect, incidental and consequential damages; and "data protection or security obligations, fraud, and infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights" to the Excluded Claims list, plus a sentence that Client's payment obligations are not subject to the cap.

Minimal: the drafter edited the single existing capitalised sentence rather than rewriting Section 12, kept the incumbent fee basis and the pre-existing gross negligence/willful misconduct carve-out, and added no obligations outside the fallback checklist. Deleting the "SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11" scope limiter does extend TrueLink's cap to matters previously uncapped, but that trade is necessary to cap Client's Agreement-wide exposure and tracks the playbook model language ("arising out of or relating to this Agreement"); worth flagging to the deal team as the concession being made.

Preserves intent: the Section 12(a) Client indemnity at p0071 is untouched and, being carved out, continues to operate uncapped; no timing, remedy or payment mechanic is disturbed, and the vendor-side gross negligence/willful misconduct carve-out survives in mutual form.

Residual point for the rationale (not a fallback failure): the base is "compensation paid for hosting and support services" rather than all fees under the Agreement. If material fees are billed outside hosting and support (e.g. per-transaction or per-report charges), consider broadening to "all fees paid or payable by Client under this Agreement" when pressing the preferred position.
